name: Forcepoint
evidence_summary: Forcepoint sources evidence managed Secure SD-WAN, cloud central management, zero-touch deployment, MultiLink resilience and security controls.
cost_model: Quote-based appliances/software/subscriptions; managed SD-WAN positioned but pricing public transparency limited.
key_differentiators: FlexEdge Secure SD-WAN combines secure SD-WAN with strong DLP and data security heritage from the wider Forcepoint portfolio.
MultiLink resilience and zero-touch deployment with cloud central management.
Strong story for buyers prioritising data security and DLP as a procurement criterion.
best_fit_for: Enterprises with strong data protection and DLP requirements (regulated industries, government).
Organisations wanting secure SD-WAN where data security is the primary decision driver.
Buyers consolidating DLP with SD-WAN under one vendor.
watch_outs: Smaller SD-WAN market presence than the leading platforms.
Full SASE platform completeness has partial public evidence; SSE module depth should be confirmed.
Managed delivery is partner-led; co-managed and white-label support require partner validation.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: AI Mesh for data security; risk-adaptive protection scores user behaviour in real time.

resilience.note: Cloud SSE with regional redundancy; Secure SD-WAN appliances deploy in HA pairs.

profile.platform_architecture: Forcepoint pairs its long-running Secure SD-WAN (NGFW heritage from Stonesoft) with the Forcepoint ONE SSE platform. Secure SD-WAN appliances cluster natively for high availability and are managed centrally through the Security Management Center, with strength in multi-link, multi-ISP branch designs. Forcepoint ONE delivers SWG, CASB and ZTNA from a cloud platform built on a security-first architecture.
profile.security_sase: Forcepoint's differentiation is data security: market-leading DLP with unified policy from endpoint to cloud, risk-adaptive protection that adjusts enforcement to user behaviour, and AI Mesh data classification. ZTNA, SWG and CASB are delivered through Forcepoint ONE with the DLP engine underneath. For data-centric and government-adjacent buyers, the data security depth is the reason to shortlist.
profile.service_support_channel: Channel-led with government and defence heritage (the Raytheon lineage shows in certifications and clearances), strong in regulated sectors. UK presence is established, with managed offers through security MSPs. Support runs 24x7 with professional services for DLP programmes, which benefit from expert deployment.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-user SSE licensing and appliance subscriptions, quote based. The Netify verdict: shortlist Forcepoint when data loss prevention is the primary driver, in regulated or government-adjacent estates, or when risk-adaptive enforcement maps to your insider-risk programme. Buyers prioritising WAN routing breadth or the largest PoP fabrics will weight other criteria more heavily.

vendor_faqs.a: One policy engine spans endpoint, network and cloud, with mature fingerprinting, OCR and exact data matching, plus risk-adaptive protection that tightens enforcement as user risk rises. Few rivals match the depth for serious data security programmes.

vendor_faqs.q: Is Forcepoint Secure SD-WAN still developed?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes. The NGFW-based Secure SD-WAN line continues with central management and native clustering, particularly strong for multi-ISP branch resilience in security-conscious estates, and it integrates with Forcepoint ONE for cloud security.

Government and public sector, defence supply chain, financial services and any organisation where data protection obligations lead the architecture. The certification heritage and DLP depth align with those procurement requirements.

shortlist_summary: Forcepoint offer FlexEdge Secure SD-WAN combining secure SD-WAN with DLP and data security capability drawn from the wider Forcepoint portfolio, and for organisations where DLP is a hard procurement requirement rather than an optional extra, that combination is meaningful. Typically shortlisted specifically for data security depth rather than as a general-purpose SD-WAN evaluation.
cost_note: Per-user SSE and appliance subscriptions; mid pricing, with DLP depth the value driver.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK delivery via security partners; government and defence heritage suits UK public sector.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: A managed SD-WAN is a service where a provider handles the deployment, configuration, monitoring and optimisation of your WAN.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Forcepoint's own SD-WAN page defines managed SD-WAN generically as something 'a provider' delivers, and does not claim Forcepoint itself designs, deploys, monitors and reports on the service end to end. The partner programme page frames managed services as certified partner revenue. No Forcepoint-operated fully managed offer was found on the vendor pages reviewed.

f03_co_managed_service.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the Secure SD-WAN product page, the NGFW product page and datasheet, the Cybersecurity Services page, the Implementation Packages page, the Technical Support Offerings datasheet and the Global Partner Program page. No description of a shared responsibility or co-managed operating model was located.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: Forcepoint Administrative Domain License enables multiple customer environments to be managed through a single management server.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: The SD-WAN Manager datasheet evidences tenant isolation and delegated administration: it also states 'Allows division of the environment into isolated configuration domains' and names MSSPs directly. Graded partial rather than yes because no evidence of branded or white-label portals was found on any page reviewed, and the partner programme page contains no MSP, MSSP, white label or multi-tenant terms.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Resources and deliverables aligned to your deployment needs and timeline
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Packaged implementation services and consulting are published, and the Cybersecurity Services page lists 'Implementation Packages for our award-winning products' and 'Data Security Consulting customized to your organization's needs'. Graded partial because the pages reviewed do not describe discovery, pilots, staging, migration runbooks or rollback plans.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: Next Generation Firewall (NGFW) appliances (both N and S-series) now have RMA support included
f07_lifecycle_management.note: Hardware replacement is included in the support contract, with an option to 'upgrade to next business day or same day RMA service'. The SD-WAN Manager datasheet adds 'Upgrades and dynamic update packages for managed devices can be automatically downloaded' and 'Remote Upgrades One-click fail-safe remote upgrade of the managed engines'. Graded partial because upgrades and patching are customer-executed platform features rather than work performed for the customer as part of a service, and no end-of-life planning service was found.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: For LTE without Wi-Fi, Forcepoint offers the 120L model with LTE support and 125L model with LTE/5G support.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: The 120 Series datasheet also states 'Optional Wi-Fi and LTE/5G connectivity' and lists supported LTE and 5G NR band tables, so integrated cellular is a shipped hardware capability. SIM management and signal monitoring specifics were not located in the pages reviewed.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: Forcepoint operates its own cloud web security service and the SWG page lists 'Public cloud elasticity' and 'Distributed enforcement' as features, but none of the pages reviewed (SWG, CASB, Forcepoint ONE, AI Mesh, Trust Center) publish gateway or point of presence infrastructure detail. Graded partial with low confidence for that reason: a firm yes would need a page describing Forcepoint operated gateway locations.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the SWG, CASB, Forcepoint ONE and AI Mesh product pages, the Secure SD-WAN page and the Trust Center. No reference to customer-hosted, dedicated or sovereign points of presence was located.

f21_private_global_backbone.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the Secure SD-WAN page, the NGFW product page and datasheet, the SWG and CASB pages and the AI Mesh page. No claim of a vendor owned or controlled inter-region backbone was located, and no national network claim was found either.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: 24/7 availability for your most critical issues.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: The Technical Support Offerings datasheet publishes tiered severity response targets ('Severity 1 1 hour' for Essential, 'Severity 1 45 minutes' for Enhanced, 'Severity 1 30 minutes' for Enterprise) and states 'Severity 1 issues use a follow-the-sun approach; Forcepoint technicians are always available'. Graded partial because these are support response commitments only: no uptime percentage, and no latency, jitter, loss or change handling commitments were found in the pages reviewed.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Forcepoint authors the NGFW software itself. The datasheet also evidences 'Anti-malware sandboxing', 'Granular application control', 'Always-on SD-WAN connectivity for enterprises' and 'URL Filtering (Separate Subscription)'. URL filtering is a chargeable subscription module but runs on the same platform rather than a separate appliance, so the grade remains yes rather than partial.

f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The Technical Support Offerings datasheet describes a reactive, severity-driven technical support model with Customer Success Manager and Customer Success Architect roles, but no 24/7 NOC or SOC monitoring the customer service, no incident ownership through to root cause analysis and no structured service review or change governance were described. Checked also the Cybersecurity Services, Implementation Packages and Global Partner Program pages.

delivery_model.quote: A managed SD-WAN is a service where a provider handles the deployment, configuration, monitoring and optimisation of your WAN.
delivery_model.note: Forcepoint authors the product (NGFW / FlexEdge Secure SD-WAN, SMC, DLP, SWG, CASB). Its own SD-WAN page describes managed SD-WAN in the third person as something 'a provider' does, and the partner programme page positions managed services as partner revenue rather than a Forcepoint-operated service. No Forcepoint-operated managed network service page was found in the pages reviewed.

underlay_ownership.quote: Slash networking costs and improve reliability with real-time mixing and matching of local ISP broadband and private MPLS selection.
underlay_ownership.note: Forcepoint's SD-WAN rides transport the customer already buys (local ISP broadband, private MPLS, and cellular via the LTE and 5G appliance models). No page reviewed shows Forcepoint selling, owning or reselling circuits or core routing.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Provide users with safe and reliable access to the internet, wherever they're located
sse_layer_ownership.note: The security stack is Forcepoint's own engineering across Forcepoint DLP, Secure Web Gateway, CASB and the NGFW software rather than a third party's technology resold under the Forcepoint name. No OEM or partner attribution for the security layer was found on any page reviewed. Confidence is medium because the quote evidences a Forcepoint branded cloud web service rather than explicitly stating in-house authorship.

regulatory_documentation.quote: ISO Statement of Applicability and SOC 2 Type II certifications and assessments
regulatory_documentation.note: Frameworks found and named with downloadable documentation: ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27017:2015, ISO/IEC 27018:2019, SOC 2 Type 2 (with separate reports listed for Forcepoint ONE, Cloud DSPM and Cloud Web), GDPR, plus a 'Forcepoint EU DORA Compliance document' and 'Covered Entity Compliance with HIPAA and Forcepoint Products'. Not found in the pages reviewed: NHS DSPT, NIS2, FedRAMP, Common Criteria, PCI DSS.

pop_count.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. No point of presence, gateway or data centre count is published on the Secure SD-WAN, SWG, CASB, Forcepoint ONE or AI Mesh pages, nor on the Trust Center. No figure could be quoted, so the value stays unknown.

sla_availability_pct.note: No availability percentage was found. The Technical Support Offerings datasheet publishes severity response times only, and the Trust Center lists a 'Forcepoint Service Status' document under continuous monitoring without stating an uptime figure. A support SLA exists but with no published percentage, so this is unknown.

sectors.healthcare.quote: Ensure HIPAA, GDPR, state, and local regulatory compliance while protecting your data, your patients, and your reputation.
sectors.healthcare.note: Forcepoint runs a dedicated healthcare industry page at /industry/healthcare-cybersecurity, and its customer index carries a story tagged Healthcare. Two material caveats. First, the healthcare customer is anonymised on the index as 'Digital-First Life Sciences Innovator', so there is no named healthcare reference. Second, all healthcare content found is data security, DLP and compliance led; nothing healthcare specific was found on the Secure SD-WAN product page or in any SD-WAN case study.

sectors.financial_services.quote: With a single hybrid agent Forcepoint offered ease of manageability, which was our key selection criterion.
sectors.financial_services.note: Strongest sector evidence found. Dedicated industry page with three named customers: Fedbank Financial Services Ltd (source of the quote), UCI and Vakifbank. The customer index separately tags Middle East Bank, FBD Insurance and HDI Seguros as Financial Services, and Emirates NBD is featured. Caveat: the named references are data security and NGFW deployments, not Secure SD-WAN deployments. Note also that the page H1 narrows to banks specifically, 'Forcepoint AI-powered Cybersecurity Solutions for Banks', while the navigation label is the broader 'Financial Services'.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Dedicated retail industry page carrying three named retail customers (Whataburger, Big Star and Genuine Parts Company) and PCI content under a 'Protect Customer PII and PCI' section. The Secure SD-WAN product page independently lists retail among its industries and names The Home Depot, CVS and Sysco on its logo wall. The graded quote is the page H1 because that page was read once and headings reproduce most reliably; the customer testimonials on it were not re-verified on a second pass.

sectors.manufacturing.note: Dedicated manufacturing industry page with three named customers quoted (ACME Brick, GG Group and Caesarstone). The customer index separately tags HUBER+SUHNER as Manufacturing, and HUBER+SUHNER is the one manufacturing reference that is also an SD-WAN deployment, cited on the Secure SD-WAN page with a '20+ Countries' and '45+ Cluster Nodes' scale figure. Graded on the H1 because that page was read once.

sectors.energy_utilities.quote: ERG Group Partners with Forcepoint to Scale with the Rising Tide of Renewable Energy
sectors.energy_utilities.note: A named, dedicated energy case study, and the customer index tags it 'Energy'. The story states an Italian headquarters and describes wind, hydroelectric and solar plants across Europe. Caveat: there is no dedicated energy or utilities industry page, this is a single reference, and it is not an SD-WAN deployment.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Defense-Grade Security for the Public Sector
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Graded yes on the dedicated industry page plus published assurance frameworks rather than on customers. The page names Common Criteria, CMMC, FIPS 140-3 and the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and refers to Federal Civilian Executive Branch Agencies. Confidence is held at medium because no government customer is named anywhere that was read, and the framing is almost entirely US federal, with no evidence found for UK, EU or other national public sector accreditation. Note the corporate positioning at source 3 also names 'defense' and 'intelligence'.

sectors.education.quote: Liberty University Secures Data at Scale to Safeguard AI Innovation
sectors.education.note: A named university with a dedicated case study, tagged Education on the customer index, and stated at more than 140,000 residential and online learners. Caveat: there is no dedicated education industry page, this is a single reference, and it is a data security rather than an SD-WAN engagement.

sectors.transport_logistics.quote: VR Group Delivers a Reliable Network Aboard High-Speed Trains
sectors.transport_logistics.note: The best evidenced sector for the SD-WAN product specifically. VR Group is a named rail operator, the story describes it as a railway transportation and maintenance company operating across Finland, and VR Group also appears as a testimonial in the 'Why Customers Choose Forcepoint's Managed SD-WAN' section of the SD-WAN product page. Caveat: no dedicated transport industry page exists, and this is rail passenger and freight rather than road logistics. Forcepoint's own customer index does not offer a Transport tag; it tags two comparable stories as 'Aerospace'.

sectors.professional_services.quote: Communisis Modernizes Their Forcepoint DLP with Risk-Adaptive Protection
sectors.professional_services.note: Deliberately not graded yes. Forcepoint publishes no professional services industry page and its customer index has no professional services tag. The only candidate is Communisis, a named UK customer described on its story page as providing communications and print management services for UK financial services and insurance firms plus creative and point-of-sale marketing. Classifying that as professional services is a Netify reading, not a Forcepoint claim, and the engagement is DLP not SD-WAN. The nearest vendor tag found is 'Information Technology' against Globaltek Security, which is a different thing again.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: Burger King Scales SD-WAN for Hundreds of Restaurants
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: A named restaurant estate customer with a dedicated SD-WAN case study, stating over 650 restaurants and a Turkish headquarters, and also quoted on the SD-WAN product page. Confidence is medium and claimed_by is recorded as a Netify assessment because the hospitality classification is ours, not Forcepoint's. Conflict recorded and not resolved: Forcepoint's own customer index tags a comparable story, 'Global Food Chain', as 'Entertainment', and its retail industry page places the quick service restaurant customer Whataburger under retail. Forcepoint therefore does not itself recognise a hospitality or leisure sector.

regions.uk_ireland.note: Graded partner_integrated because Forcepoint states at source 4 that '100% of our business flows through partners.', so nothing is delivered directly in any territory. Supporting UK and Ireland evidence: published offices at 'Reading, United Kingdom' and 'Cork, Ireland' on the contact page, reproduced identically across two reads, plus Communisis as a named UK customer. Important limitation: offices are corporate presence, not service delivery. No UK or Ireland point of presence, data centre, data residency option or public sector accreditation such as Cyber Essentials or G-Cloud was found on any page read.

regions.europe.note: Graded partner_integrated on the strength of the '100% of our business flows through partners.' statement at source 4. Europe is the best evidenced region for delivery of the SD-WAN product itself: VR Group is a live SD-WAN deployment across Finland, ERG is a named Italian energy customer with plants across Europe, Eczacibasi Holding and Burger King are Turkish customers, and the GNZ testimonial on the SD-WAN product page explicitly credits a named local partner, magellan. A Helsinki office is also published. Limitation: no European point of presence list, no data centre locations and no EU data residency statement were found.

regions.north_america.note: Graded partner_integrated rather than yes because of the unambiguous '100% of our business flows through partners.' statement at source 4, which applies to the home market too. Supporting evidence: Austin, Texas is published as the corporate headquarters, Liberty University is a named US customer, and the public sector page publishes US federal assurance frameworks including CMMC, FIPS 140-3 and the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model. The SD-WAN product page logo wall is dominated by US enterprises. Limitation: still no published point of presence or cloud region list; no FedRAMP authorisation was found on the pages read.

regions.asia_pacific.note: Graded partner_integrated per the '100% of our business flows through partners.' statement at source 4. Supporting evidence is thin: published offices at 'Mumbai, India', 'Bangalore, India', 'Singapore' and 'Hong Kong', plus one named Indian customer, Fedbank Financial Services Ltd, on the financial services page. Confidence is low because that is a single in region customer, it is a data security rather than SD-WAN reference, and no Asia Pacific point of presence, data centre or local data residency option was found. No Japan, Korea or Australia specific evidence was found at all.

regions.middle_east_africa.note: Graded partner_integrated per the '100% of our business flows through partners.' statement at source 4. Supporting evidence: published offices at 'Dubai, United Arab Emirates' and 'Riyadh, Saudi Arabia', plus the customer index featuring Emirates NBD and carrying a story tagged Financial Services titled 'Middle East Bank'. Two limitations drive the low confidence. The Middle East reference is anonymised, and the individual Emirates NBD story URL returned 404 (source 27) so it could not be read. Critically, no Africa evidence of any kind was found: no office, no customer, no partner. This grade rests entirely on the Middle East half of the region.

regions.latin_america.note: Graded partner_integrated per the '100% of our business flows through partners.' statement at source 4. Supporting evidence: published offices at 'São Paulo, Brazil' and 'Mexico City, Mexico', plus HDI Seguros, a named insurance customer tagged Financial Services. Confidence is low because the HDI Seguros story heading is generic and does not name the customer, the story is a data security rather than SD-WAN engagement, and no Latin American point of presence, data centre or in country partner was published on any page read.

regions.china_mainland.note: No mainland China evidence found and this is a firm unknown rather than a gap in searching. The nearest published location is a Hong Kong office, which is not mainland China and does not imply a mainland arrangement. Per the brief, the corporate 'across 150 countries' style claim at source 3 is a generic global statement and is treated as evidence of nothing here. Specifically checked and not found: any ICP licence, any mainland point of presence or data centre, any named Chinese carrier or in country partner, any mainland customer, and any China data residency statement. The Data Security Cloud product page at source 18 was read for exactly this and returned no infrastructure or region information at all.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: Ideal for large enterprises, campus networks and data centers.
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Clearly and repeatedly evidenced. The quote is the positioning of the 3500 Series appliance on the Secure SD-WAN page and reproduced identically across two separate reads of that page. Corroborated by the corporate positioning at source 3, 'For more than 20 years, we've protected the world's most sensitive data, across defense, intelligence, finance, healthcare and global enterprises.', by scale statistics on that page including 12k+ customers and 485 of the Forbes Global 2000, and by an SD-WAN logo wall of Coca-Cola, Visa, IBM, American Express, Intel, Delta, Citi, Kyndryl and British Airways. This is unambiguously the target.

organisation_fit.mid_market.quote: Ideal for mid-sized and large offices.
organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Deliberately graded partial, not yes. The quote is the positioning of the 2300, 2200 and 1200 Series appliances and reproduced identically across two reads. The critical distinction is that this describes the size of a site within a customer network, not the size of the buying organisation, so it is not evidence of mid-market targeting. Nothing found supports a genuine mid-market motion: no mid-market pricing, no packaged mid-market tier, no case study of an identifiably mid-sized company, and no use of the phrase mid-market anywhere on the pages read. A mid-market buyer would in practice reach Forcepoint only through a channel partner given the 100 per cent partner model at source 4.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: Ideal for remote offices, branches and stores.
organisation_fit.small_business.note: No evidence of small business targeting was found, and the quoted phrase is the reason it is unknown rather than yes. The 60, 120 and 130 Series appliances are positioned for remote offices, branches, stores and brick-and-mortar locations, all of which are sites inside a larger enterprise estate rather than small businesses as customers in their own right. Specifically checked and not found: any SMB or small business tier, any self-serve or published entry price (the pricing path at source 25 returns 404), any free trial pricing, and any small business case study. Not graded not_primary because Forcepoint nowhere explicitly rules the segment out, and inferring exclusion would be the same reasoning error as inferring inclusion.
